tob-10198: Saint Catherine of Siena was a fourteenth-century Italian mystic whose letters carried her voice into papal palaces and war camps alike. She wrote to popes, princes, and prisoners, urging repentance and church reform with startling bluntness. Vida Scudder’s translation brings these passionate letters to English readers. They show one of the boldest women of the Middle Ages in her own words.
tob-10498: James Legge’s monumental Chinese Classics series begins with the Analects, the sayings of Confucius collected by his students. These brief dialogues — on learning, virtue, government, and the gentleman’s conduct — became the textbook of Chinese civilization for two thousand years. Legge’s bilingual edition and notes made Confucian thought accessible to the English-speaking world.
tob-10798: Paul Carus retells the life and teachings of the Buddha in the language of the Gospels, drawing entirely from ancient Buddhist sources. His aim was to present Buddhism to Western readers in a form they would instantly recognize. The result became one of the most widely read introductions to the faith, translated into many languages.
tob-4098: J. Armitage Robinson’s volume binds three gems of first Christianity — the Letter of Barnabas, the Shepherd of Hermas, and the Didache. These writings show the church as it stood ere the canon shut its doors. His edition mates the old texts with a clear English rendering. Common readers may now meet Christianity’s first generations.
tob-10898: The Tale of Two Brothers is ancient Egypt’s story of the faithful Bata — betrayed, murdered, and reborn through a chain of marvels. This 3,200-year-old tale is the world’s oldest fairy story. The text is a treasure of Egyptian narrative literature.
tob-14098: R. H. Charles’s Testament of the Twelve Forefathers gives the dying speeches of Jacob’s twelve sons — soul-rede from latter-Temple Jewry. Each son warns his bairns against his own besetting sin. His Englishing opened the work to latter-day bookmen. The text lights the time’s right-living and its Messiah-hopes.
cia-0000107298: A June 1991 report, its title carrying the archive's typos, on official word that claims of missing American pilots still being alive were groundless. One by one, the sensational MIA stories of the early 1990s were knocked down by investigation. The entry shows the steady, unglamorous work of checking facts against hope.
cia-0000107498: A June 1964 report on Cuban exiles planning to march on Washington during an Organization of American States meeting. The exiles wanted to pressure the hemisphere into tougher action against Castro's Cuba. The document shows the CIA monitoring domestic protest with foreign-policy stakes — activism that could embarrass the United States before its neighbors.
cia-0000113198: Another untitled 1945 list of names and descriptions — the archive's pages as received, context stripped away. Such lists were working documents, meaningful to the officers who compiled them and opaque to everyone since. The entry is a puzzle with half its pieces missing.
cia-0000117898: An August 1980 report on an OPEC tri-ministerial conference focused on strategy. Oil ministers from three producers were coordinating — and every move rippled through Western economies. The document shows energy politics as high intelligence priority in the years after the oil shocks.
cia-0000119698: A January 1953 estimate of the likely consequences of prosecuting an anti-trust suit against certain companies — the truncated title hides which. Even domestic legal cases got the intelligence treatment when they touched national interests. The document is a reminder that estimates covered economics as well as enemies.
cia-0000124298: A December 1957 scientific report on electronics — the truncated subject hides the specific focus. Soviet electronics capabilities underpinned everything from satellites to missiles. The entry represents the technical intelligence grind: understanding the enemy one circuit at a time.
cia-0000132298: Situation Report 607: smoke from Kuwait reaching Iran — the truncated title hints at political fallout too. The oil fires' black clouds drifted across borders, choking the region. The document tracks pollution as politics: the war's smoke, crossing frontiers.
cia-0000132398: An October 1960 NSC briefing on Latin America. The hemisphere was the Cold War's near abroad — Cuba lost, others wobbling. The document surveys the backyard: the neighbors, the threats, and the plan.
cia-0000132598: Item 1 in an August 1960 general series: Khrushchev to visit Cuba, and possibly Mexico. The Soviet leader's travel plans were geopolitical theater. The document is the itinerary, rumored: the Kremlin, coming to the Caribbean.
cia-0000133198: A 1960 report: a pro-communist student group in Colombia planning demonstrations against an OAS meeting — the truncated title cuts off the details. The students were targeting the hemisphere's parliament. The document is the plan: the march, plotted.
cia-0000135798: A 1952 transcribed cable, title deleted, with a detailed summary of information on coup efforts. The plotting began two years before the fall. The document is the early scheme: the coup, conceived.
cia-0000135898: A 1954 summary of a deleted subject. The summary survives; the topic does not. The entry is the paradox: the summary, without its subject.
cia-0000136198: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for REELFOOT on ZRBRIEF's willingness to sign an MDAP pact — the truncated title cuts off at when. The military aid deal, pending signature. The entry is the willingness: the pact, near.
cia-0000136298: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN stating the requirement to keep pressure off Nicaragua — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The staging ground had to stay quiet. The document is the requirement: the pressure, kept off.
cia-0000136398: A 1954 cable requesting coverage of Jose Luis Arenas's visit to Caracas. The traveler, watched. The document is the coverage: the visit, monitored.
cia-0000136998: A 1954 cable to the senior representative in Guatemala City on preparing press material substantiating something — the truncated title cuts off what. The evidence, packaged for press. The document is the preparation: the material, readied.
cia-0000140398: A 1952 document — two subjects deleted — on military personnel trained in hypnotism. The trained, unnamed. The entry is the file: the personnel, hidden.
un-ga-res-998: UN General Assembly Resolution 998, adopted in November 1956 during the Suez Crisis — the resolution that created the first United Nations Emergency Force, history's first armed peacekeeping mission. As British, French, and Israeli forces attacked Egypt, the Assembly invented peacekeeping on the fly. The resolution is the innovation: the blue helmets, born.
un-sc-res-198: Security Council Resolution 198, adopted in 1965. The mid-sixties Council at work. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-798: Security Council Resolution 798, adopted in December 1992 — the detention camps resolution, demanding the immediate closure of all detention facilities in Bosnia and free Red Cross access. The Council confronted the reports of atrocity. The resolution is the demand: the camps, closed.
un-sc-res-1398: Security Council Resolution 1398, adopted in 2002 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1498: Security Council Resolution 1498, adopted in 2003 — aligned. The Council's business rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
un-sc-res-1598: Security Council Resolution 1598, adopted in 2005 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1798: Security Council Resolution 1798, cataloged with the year 1998 — the numbering suggests 2008, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1898: Security Council Resolution 1898, cataloged with the year 1999 — the numbering suggests 2009, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1998: Security Council Resolution 1998, cataloged with the year 2012 — the historical record places this children-in-armed-conflict resolution in July 2011, targeting attacks on schools and hospitals. The designation is kept; the catalog's date is questioned.
cia-0000132498: A 1961 CIA file titled Cuba, numbered 0000132498. The Bay of Pigs year. The entry is the folder: the island, watched — in the year of the invasion.
cia-0000135698: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135698. The exiles' Spanish record continued. The entry is the record: the papers, kept.
cia-0000136698: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136698, the archive's date uncertain. The circa papers. The entry is the circa: the dating, soft.
edict-of-nantes-1598: The Edict of Nantes of 1598 — Henri IV's decree granting France's Protestant Huguenots religious tolerance after decades of civil war. Paris is worth a mass, the converted king supposedly said — and then he bought peace with toleration. The edict is the tolerance: the wars of religion, ended — for eighty-seven years.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d98: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, November 6, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 98. London's letter. The message is the correspondence: the prime minister, writing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d198: The chargé in Turkey, Kelley, to the president, the secretary of state — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 198. Ankara's stand-in envoy reported widely. The cable is the chargé's: Kelley, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d298: The President to the ambassador in Turkey, Steinhardt, November 24 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 298. The White House wrote Ankara's envoy. The message is the envoy: Steinhardt, instructed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d398: The Secretary of State to the President, November 30, 1943 — Document 398. A second that day. The memo is the doubling: the day, busy.
arxiv-2605-08798: When an object falls straight into a black hole, it broadcasts gravitational waves — ripples in spacetime that detectors can hear. Giorgio Di Russo and Donato Bini compute that waveform for radial infall at 3.5 post-Newtonian order, an extremely precise approximation of Einstein's equations. The 2026 paper sharpens the templates detectors use to recognize such plunges.
arxiv-2605-09498: Neural processes learn distributions over functions — meta-learning for regression tasks — and spectral structure can sharpen them considerably. Xianhe Chen, Hao Chen, and Yingzhen Li build spectral transformer neural processes. The 2026 paper is meta-learning operating in the frequency domain.
arxiv-2605-09698: Data-science agents stumble when the task itself is ambiguously framed — and real users are ambiguous constantly. Josefa Lia Stoisser, Marc Boubnovski Martell, Sidsel Boldsen, and colleagues benchmark that task-framing ambiguity with Ambig-DS. The 2026 paper measures how agents handle unclear instructions.
arxiv-2605-09798: Graphs avoiding l-paths between equal-degree vertices cannot be too dense — and the proof is short and sweet. Yamaan Attwa, Matías Azócar Carvajal, Simona Boyadzhiyska, and colleagues provide it. The 2026 paper is extremal graph theory, elegantly brief.
plos-pone-0003398: Cancer biologists studied how tumor cells change their crawl in this 2008 paper. Inside three-dimensional tissue, migrating cancer cells switch between a flat mesenchymal style and a round amoeboid style with membrane blebbing. The team found two proteins, ROCK1 and LIMK2, partner up in spreading cells but not in blebbing ones, marking the machinery behind each migration mode.
plos-pone-0003498: Cell biologist Rami Hannoush filmed a developmental signal in real time in this 2008 study. The Wnt pathway stabilizes beta-catenin to steer development, and its misfiring causes cancer, so he used quantitative temporal imaging to clock exactly how that stabilization unfolds. The kinetic measurements give drug hunters a precise movie of a pathway they aim to tame.
plos-pone-0003598: Hearing researchers Nelson and Takahashi found the barn owl's echo brain keeps two channels separate in this 2008 paper. The threshold for detecting an echo and the delay that locates it are processed independently, a division of labor in one of nature's finest sonar systems. The independence reveals clean modular design in auditory computation.
plos-pone-0003698: In 2008, Nosho, Irahara, and Shima ran deep stats on a colon cancer subtype. The CpG island methylator phenotype, or CIMP, marks tumors whose DNA is heavily methylated and often carries BRAF changes. Their large-scale biostatistical analysis sharpens how CIMP is defined and what it means for patients.
plos-pone-0003798: Giorgio Gilestro found fly nerves using backup plans to cross the midline in this 2008 paper. When one guidance mechanism for axon midline crossing in Drosophila was removed, redundant systems took over. The backup wiring shows the developing nervous system refusing to leave crossing to chance.
plos-pone-0003898: Back in 2008, Vera, Iczkowski, and Wang linked chemo side effects to bladder inflammation signals. Cyclophosphamide-induced cystitis raised bladder CXCR4 and drew in responding immune factors. The pathway map points to targets for easing a painful drug side effect.
plos-pone-0003998: In 2008, Lehmann, Funston, and Owen tracked lions on a South African reserve. They mapped lion home ranges and territorial behavior across Karongwe Game Reserve. The spatial ecology data guide hands-on management of fenced big carnivores. Knowing where lions roam keeps both the lions and their neighbors safer.
plos-pone-0004098: In 2008, Prieto, Koncarevic, and Park took a protein census of malaria parasites. Their large-scale proteome scan tracked Plasmodium falciparum under drug treatment. Protein shifts revealed how the parasite answers modern medicine. The protein inventory exposes fresh drug targets for hunters.
plos-pone-0004198: In 2009, Kallio, Hakulinen, and Kallio sped up protein crystal photography prep. Polystyrene nanospheres helped stubborn proteins crystallize for structure studies. The tiny beads seeded crystals where none would grow before. The handy nucleant shortcut could unlock many more protein structures.
plos-pone-0004298: In 2009, Gazzolo, Frigiola, and Bashir tested a urine clue for birth asphyxia. Urinary S100B at birth predicted outcomes in asphyxiated full-term newborns well. The protein's level flagged brain injury risk early. The simple test could guide newborn intensive care fast.
plos-pone-0358698: The liver’s methionine cycle fuels metabolism, and the PPARγ protein helps run it. This paper mapped PPARγ-dependent and -independent regulation of methionine-cycle genes in fasted and diet-induced obese mice. The regulatory map clarifies how fasting and obesity rewire liver chemistry differently.
plos-pone-0356598: Alcohol-induced mental and behavioral disorders rarely travel alone. Drawing on Korea’s national hospital discharge injury survey, this paper mapped their comorbidities — the conditions that cluster alongside. The evidence guides doctors toward integrated treatment instead of chasing each diagnosis separately.
plos-pone-0347398: Flying taxis need networks — and green ones. This paper showed how 6G integrated perception and networking, with a dynamic sleep strategy for eVTOL wireless systems, can push the low-altitude economy toward carbon neutrality. The sleep strategy cuts energy waste during the quiet hours when the skies are empty.
plos-pone-0357098: The deep sea hides our trash. This ROV survey revealed marine litter in the Mar del Plata Submarine Canyon in the southwestern Atlantic — out of sight, hidden in the deep. The findings document how far human waste reaches, in a place almost no human will ever visit.
plos-pone-0357498: The choroid plexus — the brain’s cerebrospinal fluid factory — changes size near tumors. This paper studied choroid plexus volume variation in patients with gliomas and related tumors, linking it to tumor characteristics. The volume shifts may become a valuable new imaging marker for diagnosis and monitoring.
plos-pone-0354798: How do you measure a population’s dissatisfaction with collective decisions? ElecMeter is a proposed index for evaluating dissatisfaction in social decision-making. The metric gives democracies, committees, and organizations a rigorous way to quantify discontent instead of merely sensing it.
plos-pone-0357598: The Yangtze River Delta’s relentless urban sprawl threatens the region’s ecological foundations. This paper assessed ecological sensitivity and sustainable spatial planning across the highly urbanized plain using AHP-GIS and geodetector methods. The analysis guides urbanization that leaves room for nature to survive.
plos-pone-0355298: Social trust protects against depression — but traditional gender attitudes change the equation. This Seoul study examined social trust and depression among young adults, with traditional gender role attitudes as moderator. The interplay reveals cultural nuances that one-size-fits-all mental health models miss.
plos-pone-0356498: Smarter optimization algorithms can decarbonize supply chains. This three-term conjugate gradient method with a new descent structure tackles both unconstrained optimization and low-carbon supply chain design. The mathematics finds better solutions faster — with a smaller carbon footprint as the prize.
plos-pone-0356398: Young Zambians need sexual and reproductive health services that actually reach them. This place-based study co-produced access with young people through digital tools and vending machine-enabled innovation. The co-designed approach meets youth where they already are — on their phones and streets.
plos-pone-0355198: When food prices soar, the poor don’t just eat less — they eat worse. This paper tracked rising food prices and widening nutrition gaps in Mexico, comparing the cost of nutrient-dense foods against ultra-processed ones before, during, and after COVID-19. The price trajectories reveal exactly how the pandemic priced healthy eating out of reach for millions of Mexican families, and whether the gap has closed since.
plos-pone-0356798: Seafarers and ship crews face unique health risks with minimal support. This scoping review mapped digital health promotion, prevention, and health literacy measures available to crews on cargo and passenger ships. The review reveals a largely neglected population — and the digital tools that could reach them at sea.
plos-pone-0341298: Does feeling that society is unfair change what policies people want? This paper investigated the relationship between perceived inequality and policy preferences. The findings map how subjective experiences of unfairness — not just objective gaps — drive demand for redistribution. Democracy’s policy debates run on perceptions as much as facts.
plos-pone-0355598: Fenugreek — a valuable spice and medicinal crop — needs optimal planting geometry. This Tehuledere district study tested inter-row spacing and seed rate effects on growth, yield, and yield components in Northeast Ethiopia. The agronomic findings give farmers the spacing recipe for maximum harvest.
plos-pone-0356198: Macrophages that flip between inflammatory states reshape how triple-negative breast cancer hides from immunity. This co-culture study examined how bidirectional macrophage transitions influence the cancer cells’ immune evasion and chemotherapy response. The findings reveal the tumor microenvironment as a therapeutic target in its own right.
plos-pone-0355698: Hemodialysis patients’ gut microbiomes are profoundly disturbed — with consequences for their survival. This multi-center multi-omics study revealed the dysbiosis in hemodialysis patients. The integrated molecular portrait suggests the gut may be an underappreciated driver of dialysis patients’ poor outcomes.
plos-pone-0355998: Global Geoparks must balance beauty with conservation — and landscape quality can be measured. This paper evaluated visual landscape quality using an SBE–GIS coupled model. The combined scenic-beauty and spatial analysis gives park managers an objective basis for protecting what visitors come to see.
plos-pone-0354298: Identifying winter wheat in desert oases from space demands fusing satellite data types. This paper combined synergistic active and passive remote sensing with multi-feature optimization for wheat identification in arid oasis agriculture. The fused approach maps food production where water is life.
plos-pone-0355498: Trust in public health authorities — the currency of pandemic response — needs precise measurement. This paper measured it in the United States using item response theory. The psychometrically rigorous analysis reveals exactly where trust stands — and which Americans have lost faith.
plos-pone-0336198: A women-led community center in Tripoli, Lebanon — can it build social cohesion amid sectarian tension? This pilot randomized controlled trial tested the impact. The findings offer rare experimental evidence on whether grassroots women’s leadership can stitch divided communities together.
europmc-pmc2842698: Where climates keep shifting, life never rests. This 2010 essay by Graham Bell probes ever-shifting natural picks as the engine that renews fitness in fickle settings. The author holds that swing keeps gene mix rich. The piece frames evolution in a restless world.
europmc-pmc2843598: Trading butter fats for seed fats is old diet lore, but does it spare hearts? This 2010 pool of top-trial proof says yes for heart disease. The authors fused trial sums on heart outcomes. The blend firmed the swap's case.
europmc-pmc2880998: Brain inflammation drives many ills, and this 2010 lab study tests a calming drug. The authors show dimethylfumarate cools microglial and astrocyte inflammation by cutting nitric oxide and key immune signals. Their dish work revealed the mechanism. The finding backed a drug later used in multiple sclerosis.
europmc-pmc2881098: France launched a giant online nutrition study, and this 2010 paper introduces it. The authors describe the Nutrinet-Santé Study, a web-based project linking diet to health in tens of thousands. Their design pioneered internet epidemiology. The study became a powerhouse of nutrition evidence.
europmc-pmc2882898: Staying active keeps elders able, and this 2010 review gathers the proof. The authors survey physical activity against functional limits in older adults, tied to Canada's activity guidelines. Their synthesis backs moving more at every age. The review underpins public advice for aging well and staying independent.
europmc-pmc3002198: Farm pesticides may dull young minds. This 2010 study links pesticide exposure to attention gaps in young Mexican-American farmworker kids. The authors' findings warn their families. Their work shaped safety rules. Mothers' urine samples told the exposure story. Buffer zones around fields grew after it.
europmc-pmc3031198: Comparing species' pasts needs clever math. This 2011 paper brings a tool that compares the histories of many species at once. The authors' method handles rate differences. Their tool spread through labs. Ice ages left shared marks it can read. The method runs on standard lab computers.
europmc-pmc3091298: Exome capture got automated. This 2011 paper automates building human exome libraries ready for sequencing. The authors' pipeline slashed costs. Their method powered genomics. Robots now prep thousands of exomes. Rare-disease labs adopted it at once. The pipeline runs with minimal hands.
europmc-pmc6520498: Probing deep brain regions in primates usually means surgery, but focused ultrasound offers a gentler probe: sound waves steered through the skull to nudge specific areas. In monkeys, researchers used the technique to dial activity in deep cortical and subcortical targets up or down. The work opens a noninvasive way to test what each brain region actually does.
europmc-pmc6521998: For millions of women and girls in poorer countries, menstruation brings shame, missed school, and no clean products - yet the experience went unstudied for decades. This systematic review gathers qualitative research from low- and middle-income countries into one picture. The synthesis shows how stigma and scarce resources turn a normal bodily process into a barrier to health and equality.
europmc-pmc6559198: Bacteria can spin pure cellulose - the same stuff as plant fiber - into strong, water-loving mats. This review makes the case for bacterial cellulose as wound dressing: it keeps burns moist, lets air through, and peels off without tearing new skin. Cheap to grow and kind to tissue, the biopolymer is moving from lab curiosity toward clinic.
europmc-pmc6604998: Food poisoning has many culprits - from Salmonella to Listeria to toxin-making Staphylococcus. This review profiles the major foodborne pathogens: where they lurk, how they sicken, and what stops them. The tour covers bacteria, their toxins, and the food-safety practices that keep meals safe.
europmc-pmc6678498: Bone is endlessly rebuilt by cells called osteoclasts - and oxygen sparks help direct the teardown. This review looks at reactive oxygen species in osteoclast birth and the drug targets in these pathways. Calming oxidative signals could bring new bone-loss drugs.
europmc-pmc6692298: Nature's antibiotics - antimicrobial peptides - are scattered across hundreds of papers and patents. DRAMP 2.0 gathers them: an updated open repository of nearly 20,000 peptides, general, patented, and clinical. Drug hunters get one searchable home for molecules that kill microbes.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1198: This 2007 GAO report wades into the drug-patent fight: a world trade pact lets poor nations break patents in a health crisis, but U.S. guidance on the deal read murky. GAO says Washington's line may need sharpening. The report sits at the crossroads of pill profits and sick patients half a world away.
gao-gaoreports-b-299798: Savantage Financial Services fought a 2007 award at GAO — two case numbers, one verdict. The firm said the agency's pick was unfair; the combined ruling weighs each protest point. Money-management contracts get the same fair-play scrutiny as any federal buy.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-498: The polar weather satellites were being rebuilt mid-flight in 2007 — GAO's report says the restructuring moved ahead despite technical storms. The findings track the high-wire act. The report's tension: fix the plane while flying it, or lose the forecast.
openalex-w7204196198: Is the world ruled by no one, or by a hidden hierarchy? This international-relations paper stages the debate between anarchic and hierarchical visions of world order. The authors work through the theories, from Waltz to the neorealists, testing which picture fits. Dense but rewarding, it tackles how scholars imagine power among nations.
openalex-w7204207398: Kidney patients die most often of heart disease, and the damage starts silently. This study looks at blood markers tied to early, hidden heart remodeling in chronic kidney disease. The authors search for signals that flag trouble before symptoms. A cardiology-nephrology study chasing an early warning for the highest-risk patients.
openalex-w7204212698: Children in institutional care carry broken bonds into the classroom. This article studies how ruptured attachments shape the inner lives and schooling of children in shelters. The authors draw on psychology and education research. Tender and serious, it argues that learning cannot be separated from love.
openalex-w7125696198: Metabolic syndrome strains the heart, and faulty temperature control may add to the load. This study asked patients how well their bodies regulate heat and linked it to heart symptom burden. The authors explored an overlooked connection. A cardiology study of the thermostat's role in heart strain.
openalex-w7221083398: Bad leg arteries darken heart bypass results. This study compared bypass outcomes in patients with severe limb ischemia against those without it. The team tracked early and late results for both groups. A heart-surgery study of two vessel diseases piling onto one patient.
pmc-13472498: A 2026 study examining why AI scribes — tools that turn doctor-patient conversations into clinical notes — produce bad documentation. The authors used a netnographic approach, studying online discussions and records, to map the social and technical causes of failure. Their findings point to fixes that make these tools safer for real medical practice.
pmc-13469698: This 2026 paper reconstructs the recent colonization history of the house mouse (Mus musculus domesticus) in the Americas — "New Country for Old Mice." Genetic data trace how the species spread with human settlement. It is a vivid case of invasion biology written in DNA.
pmc-13429798: A 2026 reproductive biology paper showing that compartmentalization of DHCR7 — an enzyme in cholesterol synthesis — links 7-DHC metabolism to B-ring unsaturated steroid production in the equine fetal gonad. Fetal horse gonads make unusual steroids, and the study maps how. The work illuminates a peculiar corner of developmental endocrinology.
pmc-13392498: In this 2026 study, DNA metabarcoding revealed hidden microbiota living in the pollen reserves of honey bees from the Amazonas region. Bee bread — stored pollen — hosts a microbial world barely explored. The survey adds Amazonian detail to pollinator microbiome science.
pmc-13355398: In this 2026 study, Dnajb5 — a protein from Antarctic fish — revealed a redox-sensitive mechanism coordinating muscle regeneration through mTORC1 and HDAC4. Extreme-cold-adapted biology illuminated a general muscle repair pathway. The finding connects environmental adaptation to regenerative medicine.
pmc-13324398: A 2026 statistics paper offering a unifying guiding principle for when to adjust for multiple testing. The multiple-comparisons problem confuses even experienced researchers. The principle aims to settle the debate.
pmc-13525198: A 2026 post hoc analysis finding decreased nonvertebral fracture incidence with zoledronate use beyond three years. Longer treatment kept protecting bones. The analysis extends the evidence for continued therapy.
pmc-13452198: This 2026 cell biology paper showed acute AKT signaling increases glucose phosphorylation and glycogen contribution in hepatocytes. The insulin pathway's immediate metabolic effects were mapped. The finding details liver glucose handling.
pmc-13422298: A 2026 study developing and evaluating an in situ simulated emergency training course for junior nurses. Practice in place builds readiness. The evaluation shows it worked.
pmc-13581898: This 2026 journal entry is titled "IN THIS ISSUE!" — a table-of-contents style announcement. The brief entry preserves the issue notice. Little more can be said from the record.
pmc-13530498: This 2026 conference paper analyzed the impact of osteoarthritis on outcomes after aragonite-based scaffold implantation for knee cartilage defects. The scaffold's performance in arthritic knees was tested. The paper reports the analysis.
pmc-13554698: This 2026 paper introduced Lifestyle Medicine 3.0 — from disease prevention to human health optimization. The field's next phase is ambitious. The paper frames the evolution.
pmc-13529398: A 2026 case report of an inferior vena cava Masson's tumor — a benign vascular growth — extending into the right atrium and ventricle. The tumor's intracardiac reach was extraordinary. The case documents the resection.
pmc-13519098: A 2026 veterinary paper on the temporal impact of hypothyroidism on porcine fetal growth and skeletal development. The thyroid-deficient fetuses' development was tracked. The timing effects are the finding.
pmc-13517098: A 2026 sports psychology exploratory study on opponent knowledge and competitive level effects on decision-making cognition in high school kendo athletes. The martial artists' minds were probed. The study maps the cognitive processes.
pmc-13482298: In this 2026 immunology paper, ryanodine receptor 1 proved dispensable for CD4+ T-cell differentiation and effector function in intestinal inflammation models. The calcium channel wasn't needed. The dispensability is the surprise.
pmc-13449298: This 2026 COPD paper examined alpha-SMA, NOX4, fibronectin, and HIF-1alpha in pulmonary microvascular remodeling in patients without pulmonary arterial hypertension. The vessel remodeling markers were profiled. The role is the finding.
pmc-13428698: In this 2026 computational chemistry paper (the record's title is garbled with LaTeX code), DFT-guided Lennard-Jones parametrization was developed for accurate molecular simulation. The force field parameters were quantum-guided. The parametrization is the advance.
pmc-13411298: This 2026 paper found blunted reward responsiveness during social feedback associated with peer victimization and anhedonia in socially anxious adolescents. The bullied teens' reward systems were dampened. The association is the mechanism.
pmc-13403298: A 2026 paper on mechanisms underlying pain avoidance in complex regional pain syndrome. The avoidance behavior's mechanisms were probed. The mechanisms inform therapy.
pmc-13434298: A 2026 oncology review: "Signaling Under Stress" — targeting the glucocorticoid receptor in cancer. The stress hormone receptor's cancer role was surveyed. The targeting is the therapeutic angle.
pmc-13454698: A 2026 paper on genetic mechanisms for size- and light-dependent reproductive maturation in two maple species. The trees' maturation genetics were decoded. The mechanisms are the evolutionary insight.
pmc-13510598: A 2026 review: "The Nucleolus in Human Disease" — ribosome biogenesis, nucleolar surveillance, and therapeutic opportunities. The cell's ribosome factory in disease was surveyed. The review is the synthesis.
pmc-13435998: A 2026 qualitative paper exploring motivations behind self-harm adolescents' avoidance of psychological support techniques — the absence of digital intervention. The teens' avoidance was understood. The exploring guides outreach.
pmc-13639698: This 2026 nationwide study examined the association between coexisting dementia and mortality in patients receiving oral EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (the title is truncated). The dementia-mortality link was quantified. The association informs oncology.
pmc-13498598: A 2026 paper on the leaching mechanism and behavior of rare earth elements from roasted coal gangue using citric acid. The waste's rare earths were recovered. The mechanism informs recycling.
pmc-13439098: A 2026 paper: high risk of hypoxemic COVID-19 pneumonia in myasthenia gravis patients with type I interferon autoantibodies. The autoantibodies predicted the severe pneumonia. The risk is the clinical warning.
pmc-13426098: A 2026 materials paper on data-driven design of self-adhesive epidermal electrodes and sensors. The skin electronics were optimized. The design is the wearable advance.
pmc-13464098: This 2026 editorial addressed nutrition and oral microbiology — integrative perspectives for improved oral health. The diet-mouth microbe link was framed. The editorial is the perspective.
arxiv-2606-15998: Search engines re-rank documents to show the most relevant ones first, often using entity labels like person or company names. arxiv-2606-16098: Bending light around corners on a chip is a core problem in photonics, especially on platforms where the refractive-index contrast is low. This paper optimizes waveguide bend designs for such materials, cutting light loss at the turns. It targets engineers building compact optical circuits on low-contrast platforms.
arxiv-2606-16598: Chill atoms in light jails can ape weird stuff — guard-edge phases and all. This look-back rounds up how such chill packs ape those phases, in lab and in math. A door-opener for new hands who'd steer chill-atom fakes. Old hands may skim for gaps.
